title.zh: 卷322 列傳一百九 窦光鼐 李漱芳 范宜宾 曹锡宝 谢振定 钱沣 尹壮图
title.en: Volume 322 Biographies 109: Dou Guangnai, Li Shufang, Fan Yibin, Cao Xibao, Xie Zhending, Qian Feng, Yin Zhuangtu
title.raw: 卷322 列傳一百九 窦光鼐 李漱芳 范宜宾 曹锡宝 谢振定 钱沣 尹壮图

sentences.zh: =竇光鼐=竇光鼐，字元調，山東諸城人。

translations.literal: Dou Guangnai, styled Yuandiao, was a native of Zhucheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Guangnai, whose courtesy name was Yuandiao, came from Zhucheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年進士，選庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the seventh year of the Qianlong reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after completing his term there was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考四等，罰俸。

translations.literal: On the grand examination he received grade four and was fined salary.
translations.idiomatic: On the triennial evaluation he was graded fourth class and fined a portion of his salary.

sentences.zh: 高宗夙知光鼐，居數月，擢左中允。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor had long known Guangnai; after several months he was promoted to Left Vice Director of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had long been acquainted with him; within a few months he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in due course to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In his twentieth year of service he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 督浙江學政。

translations.literal: He supervised education in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of education in Zhejiang as provincial education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，臨海縣訓導章知鄴將獻詩，光鼐以詩拙阻之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor made a southern tour, Zhang Zhiying, instructor of Linhai County, was about to present a poem; Guangnai stopped him on the grounds that the poem was crude.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial southern tour, Zhang Zhiying, the county instructor of Linhai, prepared to present a poem to the throne; Guangnai blocked him, judging the verse too poor.

sentences.zh: 知鄴欲訐光鼐，光鼐以聞。

translations.literal: Zhiying wished to impeach Guangnai; Guangnai reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiying tried to impeach Guangnai, who reported the matter to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上召知鄴試以詩，詩甚拙，且言原從軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Zhiying to test him with poetry; the poem was very crude, and he also said he had originally wished to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Zhiying and tested him with a poem; the verse was wretched, and he admitted he had once hoped to enter military service.

sentences.zh: 上斥其妄，命奪職戍闢展。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him for presumption and ordered his dismissal from office and exile to Bichan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor denounced his effrontery, stripped him of office, and sent him into exile at Bichan.

sentences.zh: 後數年，上欲赦知鄴還，而知鄴妄為悖逆語，欲以陷光鼐，上乃誅之。

translations.literal: Several years later the Emperor wished to pardon Zhiying and recall him; but Zhiying uttered reckless and rebellious words, intending to frame Guangnai, whereupon the Emperor had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the Emperor considered pardoning Zhiying and recalling him, but Zhiying spoke treasonous words in an attempt to entrap Guangnai, and the Emperor had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 光鼐學政任滿，還京師。

translations.literal: When Guangnai's term as education commissioner expired, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his term as Zhejiang education commissioner ended, Guangnai returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 秋讞，光鼐以廣西囚陳父悔守田禾殺賊，不宜入情實；

translations.literal: At the autumn assizes Guangnai held that Chen Fu, a prisoner from Guangxi who had repented and killed a bandit while guarding his crop, should not be entered as a capital case;
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn assizes Guangnai argued that Chen Fu of Guangxi, who had killed a thief while guarding his standing grain after repenting of earlier wrongdoing, should not be classified as a capital case;

sentences.zh: 貴州囚羅阿扛逞兇殺人，不宜入緩決：持異議，簽商刑部，語忿激。

translations.literal: Luo Agang, a prisoner from Guizhou who had murdered in wanton violence, should not be entered for deferred execution: he held dissenting views, endorsed them for discussion with the Board of Punishments, and his language was vehement.
translations.idiomatic: and that Luo Agang of Guizhou, who had murdered in deliberate brutality, should not be entered for deferred execution. He dissented, signed his views for consultation with the Board of Punishments, and spoke with angry vehemence.

sentences.zh: 刑部遽以聞，上命大學士來保、史貽直，協辦大學士梁詩正覆覈，請如刑部議，且言光鼐先已畫題，何得又請改擬。

translations.literal: The Board of Punishments hastily reported this; the Emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Laibao and Shi Yizhi, with assisting Grand Secretary Liang Shizheng, to review the cases. They requested approval of the Board's proposal and said that Guangnai had already signed the draft—how could he again ask for revision?
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Punishments hurriedly reported the matter. The Emperor ordered Grand Secretaries Laibao and Shi Yizhi, together with assisting Grand Secretary Liang Shizheng, to reexamine the cases. They recommended following the Board's decision and noted that Guangnai had already signed the draft—how could he now ask that it be revised?

sentences.zh: 上詰光鼐，光鼐言：「兩案異議，本屬簽商，並非固執。

translations.literal: The Emperor interrogated Guangnai. Guangnai said: "Dissent in both cases was originally a matter for endorsed consultation, not obstinate insistence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor questioned Guangnai, who replied: "My objections in both cases were meant for signed consultation, not stubborn obstruction.

sentences.zh: 因會議時言詞過激，刑部遽將簽出未定之稿先行密奏。

translations.literal: Because my language at the conference was too heated, the Board of Punishments hastily forwarded the endorsed but undecided draft in a secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Because my words at the conference were too sharp, the Board of Punishments hastily submitted the endorsed but still undecided draft in a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣未能降心抑氣，與刑部婉言，咎實難辭，請交部嚴加議處。」

translations.literal: I was unable to humble myself and soften my tone to speak gently with the Board of Punishments; the blame is hard to avoid, and I beg that it be referred to the ministry for strict disciplinary action."
translations.idiomatic: I failed to restrain my temper and speak courteously with the Board of Punishments. The fault is truly mine, and I ask that the matter be referred to the ministry for strict punishment."

sentences.zh: 上以「會讞大典，光鼐意氣自用，甚至紛呶謾罵而不自知。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At the great assize conference Guangnai was self-willed in spirit, even wrangling and hurling abuse without being aware of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor declared: "At the great assize conference Guangnai acted on wounded pride, quarreling and even hurling abuse without realizing it.

sentences.zh: 設將來預議者尤而效之，於國憲朝章不可為訓」。

translations.literal: If future participants in deliberation take this as a model, it cannot serve as instruction for the laws of the state and the regulations of the court."
translations.idiomatic: If future deliberators follow his example, it will set a ruinous precedent for the laws of the realm and the discipline of the court."

sentences.zh: 命下部嚴議，當左遷，仍命留任。

translations.literal: He ordered the ministry to deliberate strictly; demotion was appropriate, yet he still ordered him to remain at his post.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ministry to deliberate strictly; demotion was called for, yet Guangnai was allowed to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 光鼐疏言：「事主殺竊盜，律止杖徒。

translations.literal: Guangnai memorialized: "When a householder kills a thief, the statute provides only beating and penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai memorialized: "When a householder kills a thief, the code provides only beating or penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 近來各省多以竊盜拒捕而被殺，比罪人不拒捕而擅殺，皆以鬥論，寬竊盜而嚴事主，非禁暴之意。

translations.literal: In recent years many provinces have treated thieves killed while resisting arrest as comparable to offenders killed without resisting—both judged as combat, lenient toward thieves and harsh toward householders, which is not the intent of suppressing violence.
translations.idiomatic: Lately many provinces have treated a thief killed while resisting arrest the same as an offender killed without resistance—both as cases of mutual combat—thereby lenient toward thieves and harsh toward householders, which defeats the purpose of restraining violence.

sentences.zh: 應請遵本律。」

translations.literal: I request that the original statute be followed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the original statute be followed."

sentences.zh: 議行。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上以光鼐迂拙，不勝副都御史，命署內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Emperor considered Guangnai dull and impractical, unfit for Vice Censor-in-Chief, and ordered him to serve as acting Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the Emperor judged Guangnai too rigid and impractical for the vice censorate and appointed him acting Grand Secretary of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 授順天府府尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 坐屬縣蝗不以時捕，左遷四品京堂，仍留任。

translations.literal: For locusts in subordinate counties not being caught in time, he was demoted to a fourth-rank capital office, yet remained at his post.
translations.idiomatic: Because locusts in his subordinate counties were not destroyed in time, he was demoted to a fourth-rank capital post but kept in office.

sentences.zh: 旋赴三河、懷柔督捕蝗，疏言：「近京州縣多旗地，嗣後捕蝗，民為旗地佃，當一體撥夫應用。」

translations.literal: Soon he went to Sanhe and Huairou to supervise locust-catching and memorialized: "Near the capital many counties have banner lands; hereafter in catching locusts, when commoners are tenants on banner lands, laborers should be allocated equally.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to Sanhe and Huairou to supervise locust eradication and memorialized: "Near the capital many counties contain banner estates; hereafter, when commoners who tenant banner land join in locust campaigns, labor should be levied from them on the same footing as others."

sentences.zh: 上從所請，以諭直隸總督楊廷璋。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted the request and so instructed Zhili Governor-General Yang Tingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the request and relayed it to Zhili Governor-General Yang Tingzhang.

sentences.zh: 廷璋言自方觀承始設護田夫，旗、民均役。

translations.literal: Tingzhang said that from the time of Fang Guancheng field-guard laborers had been established, with bannermen and commoners serving equally.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhang replied that field-guard laborers had been instituted under Fang Guancheng, with bannermen and commoners sharing the burden equally.

sentences.zh: 上復以詰光鼐，召還京師，令從軍機大臣入見。

translations.literal: The Emperor again interrogated Guangnai, recalled him to the capital, and ordered him to enter audience with the Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again pressed Guangnai, recalled him to the capital, and ordered him to appear before the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 問：「民為旗地佃，不肯撥夫應用，屬何人莊業？」

translations.literal: He asked: "When commoners are tenants on banner lands and refuse to supply laborers, whose estate does this belong to?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "When commoners tenant banner land and refuse to furnish labor, whose estate is involved?

sentences.zh: 光鼐不能對，請徵東北二路同知及三河、順義知縣質證。

translations.literal: Guangnai could not answer and requested that the sub-prefects of the northeast two routes and the magistrates of Sanhe and Shunyi be summoned to testify.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai could not answer and asked that the sub-prefects of the northeast routes and the magistrates of Sanhe and Shunyi be summoned to testify.

sentences.zh: 退又疏請罷護田夫，別定派夫捕蝗事例。

translations.literal: On retiring he again memorialized requesting abolition of field-guard laborers and separate regulations for allocating laborers to catch locusts.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing he memorialized again to abolish field-guard laborers and establish separate rules for levying men to catch locusts.

sentences.zh: 上以光鼐所見迂鄙紕繆，下部議，奪職。

translations.literal: The Emperor deemed Guangnai's views crude, erroneous, and confused; referred him to the ministry for deliberation and deprived him of office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged Guangnai's views crude and confused, referred the matter to the ministry, and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 居數月，諭光鼐但拘鈍無能，無大過，左授通政司副使。

translations.literal: After several months he indicated that Guangnai was merely dull and incompetent, without grave fault, and demoted him to left vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: After a few months the Emperor ruled that Guangnai was merely slow-witted and inept, not guilty of grave misconduct, and demoted him to Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 再遷宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 复督浙江學政，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He again supervised education in Zhejiang and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Zhejiang education commissioner and promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 浙江州縣倉庫多虧缺，上命察覈。

translations.literal: Zhejiang's prefectures and counties had many deficits in granaries and treasuries; the Emperor ordered investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries and treasuries throughout Zhejiang showed heavy deficits, and the Emperor ordered an audit.

sentences.zh: 光鼐疏言：「前總督陳輝祖、巡撫王亶望貪墨敗露，總督富勒渾未嚴察。

translations.literal: Guangnai memorialized: "Former Governor-General Chen Huizu and Governor Wang Danwang were exposed for corruption; Governor-General Fulehun did not investigate strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai memorialized: "Former Governor-General Chen Huizu and Governor Wang Danwang were exposed for corruption, yet Governor-General Fulehun did not investigate rigorously.

sentences.zh: 臣聞嘉興、海鹽、平陽諸縣虧數皆逾十萬，當察覈分別定擬。」

translations.literal: I hear that deficits in Jiaxing, Haiyan, Pingyang, and other counties all exceed one hundred thousand; investigation and separate adjudication are needed."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that shortfalls in Jiaxing, Haiyan, Pingyang, and other counties each exceed one hundred thousand taels; they should be audited and adjudicated separately."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其持正，命尚書曹文埴、侍郎姜晟往會巡撫伊齡阿及光鼐察覈。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his uprightness and ordered Minister Cao Wenhan and Vice Minister Jiang Sheng to proceed and join Governor Yiling'a and Guangnai in investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his integrity and sent Minister Cao Wenhan and Vice Minister Jiang Sheng to join Governor Yiling'a and Guangnai in the audit.

sentences.zh: 旋疏劾永嘉知縣席世維借諸生穀輸倉；

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized impeaching Xi Shiwei, magistrate of Yongjia, for borrowing grain from licentiates to fill the granary;
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized against Xi Shiwei, magistrate of Yongjia, for borrowing grain from licentiates to fill the public granary;

sentences.zh: 平陽知縣黃梅假彌虧苛斂，且於母死日演劇；

translations.literal: Huang Mei, magistrate of Pingyang, for falsely claiming deficits and levying harsh exactions, and moreover performing opera on the day of his mother's death;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mei, magistrate of Pingyang, for fabricating deficits to justify harsh levies and staging an opera on the day his mother died;

sentences.zh: 仙居知縣徐延翰斃臨海諸生馬寘於獄；

translations.literal: Xu Yanhan, magistrate of Xianju, for beating to death the Linhai licentiate Ma Zhen in prison;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanhan, magistrate of Xianju, for beating the Linhai licentiate Ma Zhen to death in prison;

sentences.zh: 並及布政使盛住上年詣京師，攜貲過豐，召物議；

translations.literal: and also involving Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Zhu, who last year went to the capital carrying excessively abundant funds, provoking public talk;
translations.idiomatic: and also Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Zhu, who on his journey to the capital the previous year carried an suspiciously large sum of money, arousing gossip;

sentences.zh: 總督富勒渾經嘉興，供應浩煩，餽閽役數至千百。

translations.literal: and Governor-General Fulehun passing through Jiaxing with lavish provisions, tipping gate servants by the hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: and Governor-General Fulehun, who while passing through Jiaxing demanded extravagant hospitality and tipped gate servants by the hundreds and thousands.

sentences.zh: 上命大學士阿桂如浙江按治。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui to proceed to Zhejiang to investigate and settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui to go to Zhejiang and conduct a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疏言盛住詣京師，附攜應解參價銀三萬九千馀，非私貲；

translations.literal: Agui memorialized that when Sheng Zhu went to the capital he carried along over thirty-nine thousand taels of ginseng-price silver due for remittance—not private goods;
translations.idiomatic: Agui reported that Sheng Zhu had carried more than thirty-nine thousand taels of ginseng-price silver due for remittance to the capital, not private wealth;

sentences.zh: 平陽知縣黃梅母九十生日演劇，即以其夕死；

translations.literal: Huang Mei of Pingyang had opera performed for his mother's ninetieth birthday, and she died that very evening;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mei of Pingyang had staged an opera for his mother's ninetieth birthday, and she died that same night;

sentences.zh: 仙居諸生馬寘誣寺僧博，復與鬥毆，因下獄死。

translations.literal: the Xianju licentiate Ma Zhen had falsely accused a temple monk of gambling, then fought with him, and died in prison as a result.
translations.idiomatic: the licentiate Ma Zhen of Xianju had falsely accused a temple monk of gambling, fought with him, and died in custody as a result.

sentences.zh: 光鼐語皆不仇。

translations.literal: None of Guangnai's statements matched.
translations.idiomatic: None of Guangnai's charges matched the facts as Agui found them.

sentences.zh: 光鼐再疏論梅事，言阿桂遣屬吏詣平陽諮訪，未得實，躬赴平陽覆察。

translations.literal: Guangnai again memorialized on Mei's case, saying Agui had sent subordinate officials to Pingyang to inquire but had not obtained the facts, and that he personally went to Pingyang to reinvestigate.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai memorialized again on Huang Mei, saying Agui's subordinates had inquired in Pingyang without uncovering the truth, and that he had gone there himself to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 伊齡阿再疏劾光鼐赴平陽刑迫求佐證諸狀，上責光鼐乖張瞀亂，命奪職，逮下刑部。

translations.literal: Yiling'a again memorialized impeaching Guangnai for going to Pingyang and using torture to extract supporting testimony; the Emperor rebuked Guangnai as perverse and confused, ordered deprivation of office, and had him arrested and sent to the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yiling'a memorialized again, accusing Guangnai of going to Pingyang and using torture to force testimony. The Emperor denounced him as reckless and muddled, stripped him of office, and sent him to the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 光鼐尋奏：「親赴平陽，士民呈梅派捐單票，田一畝捐大錢五十；

translations.literal: Guangnai soon memorialized: "I went personally to Pingyang; gentry and commoners presented Mei's levy receipts—a levy of fifty large cash per mu;
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai soon reported: "I went to Pingyang in person; local gentry and commoners presented Huang Mei's levy receipts, showing a levy of fifty large cash per mu of land;

sentences.zh: 又勒捐富戶數至千百貫；

translations.literal: he also forced contributions from wealthy households amounting to hundreds and thousands of strings;
translations.idiomatic: he also extorted contributions from wealthy households running to hundreds and thousands of strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 每歲採買倉穀不予值。

translations.literal: each year he purchased granary grain without payment.
translations.idiomatic: each year he requisitioned granary grain without paying for it.

sentences.zh: 梅在縣八年，所侵穀值及捐錢不下二十萬。

translations.literal: Mei had been in the county eight years; grain embezzled and levied money totaled no less than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In eight years as magistrate Mei had embezzled grain and extorted levies worth no less than two hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 母死不欲發喪，特令演劇。」

translations.literal: When his mother died he did not wish to hold the funeral and specially ordered opera performed."
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he delayed the funeral and instead ordered an opera staged."

sentences.zh: 上以光鼐呈單票有據，時阿桂已​​還京師，令復如浙江秉公按治，並命江蘇巡撫閔鶚元會讞，以光鼐質證。

translations.literal: The Emperor, finding Guangnai's presented receipts well founded—Agui had already returned to the capital—ordered him again to proceed to Zhejiang for impartial investigation, and also ordered Jiangsu Governor Min E'yuan to join in judgment, using Guangnai to testify.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor found Guangnai's receipts convincing. Agui had already returned to the capital, so Guangnai was sent back to Zhejiang to investigate impartially, with Jiangsu Governor Min E'yuan to join the trial and take Guangnai's testimony.

sentences.zh: 阿桂、鶚元疏言梅婪索事實，論如律。

translations.literal: Agui and E'yuan memorialized that Mei's extortion was established fact and judgment followed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Agui and Min E'yuan reported that Huang Mei's extortion was proved and sentenced him according to law.

sentences.zh: 上以光鼐所奏非妄，命署光祿寺卿，阿桂、文埴、晟、伊齡阿皆下部議。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that Guangnai's reports were not false, appointed him acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and referred Agui, Wenhan, Sheng, and Yiling'a all to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ruled that Guangnai's charges were not groundless, appointed him acting Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and referred Agui, Cao Wenhan, Jiang Sheng, and Yiling'a to the ministry for disciplinary review.

sentences.zh: 旋擢光鼐宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: Soon Guangnai was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 复督浙江學政。

translations.literal: He again supervised education in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Zhejiang education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再遷左都御史。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六十年，充會試正考官，榜發，首歸安王以铻，次王以銜，兄弟聯名高第。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he served as chief examiner for the metropolitan examination; when the list was published, first came Wang Yiyue of Gui'an, second Wang Yixian—the brothers ranked at the top together.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he served as chief metropolitan examiner; when the results were announced, Wang Yiyue of Gui'an placed first and Wang Yixian second—the brothers topping the list together.

sentences.zh: 大學士和珅素嫉光鼐，言於上，謂光鼐迭為浙江學政，事有私。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Heshen had long resented Guangnai and spoke to the Emperor, saying that because Guangnai had repeatedly served as Zhejiang education commissioner, there was favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Heshen, who had long resented Guangnai, told the Emperor that because Guangnai had repeatedly held the Zhejiang education post, the examination had been tainted by favoritism.

sentences.zh: 上命解任聽部議，及廷試，和珅為讀卷官，以銜復以第一人及第，事乃解。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him removed pending ministry deliberation; at the palace examination Heshen served as reader of papers, and Yixian again placed first—whereupon the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Guangnai removed pending ministry review; at the palace examination Heshen served as reader of papers, and Wang Yixian again placed first, clearing the suspicion.

sentences.zh: 命予四品銜休致。

translations.literal: He was granted fourth-rank title and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a fourth-rank honorary title and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =李漱芳=李漱芳，字藝圃，四川渠縣人。

translations.literal: Li Shufang, styled Yipu, was a native of Quxian in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shufang, whose courtesy name was Yipu, came from Quxian in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the twenty-second year of the Qianlong reign and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授河南道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed investigating censor for the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In his thirty-third year of service he was appointed investigating censor for the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡視中城，尚書福隆安家奴藍大恃勢縱恣，挾無賴酗酒，橫行市肆間。

translations.literal: While inspecting the central city he found that Lan Da, a household slave of Minister Fulong'an, relied on power to run riot, bringing ruffians to drink and swagger through the markets.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the central city he found Lan Da, a bondservant in Minister Fulong'an's household, abusing his master's power, gathering ruffians to drink, and terrorizing the markets.

sentences.zh: 漱芳捕治，論奏，高宗深嘉之，命戍藍大，以福隆安下吏議。

translations.literal: Shufang arrested and punished him and memorialized; the Gaozong Emperor deeply praised this and ordered Lan Da exiled, and Fulong'an referred to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Shufang arrested and punished him and memorialized the case; Emperor Gaozong greatly approved, ordered Lan Da exiled, and referred Fulong'an to the ministry for review.

sentences.zh: 尋擢工科給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to supervising secretary of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Wang Lun of Shouzhang raised a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year Wang Lun of Shouzhang led a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 漱芳疏陳奸民聚眾滋事，為飢寒所迫；

translations.literal: Shufang memorialized that wicked commoners gathering to make trouble were driven by hunger and cold;
translations.idiomatic: Shufang memorialized that the rioters had gathered because hunger and cold had driven them to it;

sentences.zh: 又言近畿亦有流民扶老攜幼，遷徙逃亡，有司監盧溝橋，阻不使北行。

translations.literal: he also said that near the capital there were also refugees supporting the old and carrying the young, migrating and fleeing, while officials guarded Lugou Bridge and blocked them from going north.
translations.idiomatic: he also reported refugees near the capital supporting the elderly and carrying children as they fled, while officials at Lugou Bridge blocked their northward passage.

sentences.zh: 給事中範宜賓亦以為言，請增設粥廠。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Fan Yibin also spoke similarly and requested additional gruel kitchens.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Fan Yibin made the same argument and asked that more relief kitchens be opened.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎高樸、袁守侗率宜賓、漱芳往盧溝橋及近畿諸城鎮省視，初無流民。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Vice Ministers Gao Pu and Yuan Shoutong to lead Yibin and Shufang to inspect Lugou Bridge and townships near the capital; initially there were no refugees.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Vice Ministers Gao Pu and Yuan Shoutong, with Fan Yibin and Shufang, to inspect Lugou Bridge and nearby towns; at first they found no refugees.

sentences.zh: 倫亂定，俘其徒檻致京師廷鞫，命漱芳旁視，無言為飢寒迫者。

translations.literal: When Lun's rebellion was pacified, his followers were caged and brought to the capital for court interrogation; the Emperor ordered Shufang to observe; none said they had been driven by hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lun's rebellion was suppressed, his followers were brought to the capital in cages for interrogation; Shufang was ordered to watch, but none claimed hunger or cold had forced them into revolt.

sentences.zh: 問歲事，對秋收尚及半。

translations.literal: Asked about the year's harvest, they answered that autumn crops were still at least half complete.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the harvest, they replied that the autumn crop was still at least half intact.

sentences.zh: 上責漱芳妄言，代奸民解說，心術不可問，不宜复居言路，為世道人心害，宥罪，降禮部主事。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Shufang for false statements, speaking on behalf of wicked commoners; his motives were questionable, he should not again hold a remonstrance post, harmful to society and men's hearts—his crime was pardoned but he was demoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Shufang for reckless speech, saying he had spoken for wicked men and that his motives were suspect; he should not again hold a remonstrance post lest he harm public morals. His life was spared, but he was demoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，禮部請以漱芳升授員外郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year the Ministry of Rites requested promoting Shufang to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year the Ministry of Rites nominated Shufang alone for promotion to vice director.

sentences.zh: 故事，郎中、員外郎員缺，選應升授者，擬正、陪上請。

translations.literal: By precedent, when director and vice director posts were vacant, those eligible for promotion were nominated as primary and alternate and submitted for approval.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when director or vice director posts fell vacant, eligible candidates were nominated as primary and alternate choices for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 至是，獨以漱芳請。

translations.literal: On this occasion only Shufang was nominated.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion only Shufang was put forward.

sentences.zh: 上不懌，責尚書永貴擅專邀譽，涉明季黨援朋比之習，奪其職。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased, rebuked Minister Yonggui for acting on his own to seek reputation, involving the Ming-dynasty habit of factional patronage and cliquishness, and deprived him of office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased, accused Minister Yonggui of acting on his own to win favor, and said the nomination smacked of late-Ming factional patronage; Yonggui was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 漱芳久之乃遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Only after a long time did Shufang transfer to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Only much later was Shufang promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =範宜賓=範宜賓，漢軍鑲黃旗人，大學士文程後也。

translations.literal: Fan Yibin, a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was a descendant of Grand Secretary Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yibin, a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was a descendant of Grand Secretary Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 以廕生官戶部郎中，歷御史給事中，累遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he held the post of director in the Ministry of Revenue, served as censor and supervising secretary, and was promoted in succession to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he became a director in the Ministry of Revenue, served as censor and supervising secretary, and rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 出為安徽布政使，與巡撫胡文伯不相能，兩江總督高晉以聞。

translations.literal: He went out as Anhui provincial administration commissioner; he did not get along with Governor Hu Wenbo, and Liangjiang Governor-General Gao Jin reported this.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Anhui provincial administration commissioner but clashed with Governor Hu Wenbo; Liangjiang Governor-General Gao Jin reported the friction to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上召宜賓還，授左副都御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor recalled Yibin and appointed him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Fan Yibin and appointed him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 宜賓奏言屬縣蝗見，屢請捕治，文伯執不可。

translations.literal: Yibin memorialized that locusts had appeared in subordinate counties; he repeatedly requested catching them, but Wenbo stubbornly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yibin reported locusts in his subordinate counties and repeatedly asked that they be destroyed, but Hu Wenbo obstinately refused.

sentences.zh: 上為黜文伯，而宜賓亦以捕蝗不力下吏議，當左遷。

translations.literal: The Emperor dismissed Wenbo for this, but Yibin also was referred to the ministry for ineffective locust-catching and should be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dismissed Hu Wenbo on this account, but Fan Yibin was also referred to the ministry for failing to control the locusts effectively and was due for demotion.

sentences.zh: 上以宜賓舊為御史尚黽勉，命仍為御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor, recalling that Yibin had formerly been a censor and was still diligent, ordered him to remain a censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, remembering Yibin's earlier service as a censor and his continued diligence, allowed him to keep that post.

sentences.zh: 宜賓疏言籓臬有所陳奏，輒呈稿督撫，當禁飭。

translations.literal: Yibin memorialized that when provincial officials submitted memorials they always presented drafts first to governors-general and governors, and that this should be forbidden and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yibin memorialized that when provincial officials memorialized the throne they habitually showed their drafts first to governors-general and governors, a practice that should be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 上以整飭吏治，要在朝廷綱紀肅清，自無扶同蒙蔽之事，不在設法峻防，置其議不行。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that to rectify official conduct the key lay in keeping court discipline clear; there would naturally be no collusion to conceal wrongdoing, and harsh preventive measures were unnecessary—Yibin's proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied that sound governance depended on discipline at court, not on elaborate safeguards against collusion; Yibin's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 及與漱芳同被譴，上以宜賓漢軍世僕，乃敢妄言幹譽，特重其罰，奪職，戍新疆。

translations.literal: When he suffered punishment together with Shufang, the Emperor said that as a Han Banner bondservant by birth Yibin had dared to speak recklessly to win reputation; his penalty was especially severe—deprivation of office and exile to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Punished together with Shufang, Fan Yibin was judged more harshly because, as a Han Banner bondservant by birth, he had dared speak recklessly for reputation; he was stripped of office and exiled to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: =曹錫寶=曹錫寶，字鴻書，一字劍亭，江南上海人。

translations.literal: Cao Xibao, styled Hongshu and also Jianting, was a native of Shanghai in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xibao, whose courtesy names were Hongshu and Jianting, came from Shanghai in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，以舉人考授內閣中書，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: In early Qianlong, as a provincial graduate he passed examination and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat, serving as a clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianlong reign he entered service through the provincial graduate route as a Grand Secretariat secretary and Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 資深當擢侍讀，錫寶辭。

translations.literal: When seniority entitled him to promotion to reader, Xibao declined.
translations.idiomatic: When seniority made him eligible for promotion to reader, Xibao declined.

sentences.zh: 大學士傅恆知其欲以甲科進，乃不為請遷。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Fu Heng knew he wished to advance through the jinshi examination and therefore did not request his transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fu Heng, knowing he hoped to rise through the jinshi examination, did not seek a promotion for him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，成進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he passed the jinshi examination and became a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he passed the jinshi examination and became a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸，病瘍，數年乃愈。

translations.literal: He returned home on his mother's death, fell ill with ulcers, and was several years recovering.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his mother's mourning, was stricken with ulcers, and took several years to recover.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，散館，改刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, upon leaving the academy, he was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, after leaving the Hanlin Academy, he was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 授山東糧道。

translations.literal: He was appointed grain intendant of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grain intendant of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 衛千總寧廷言子惠以索逋殺千總張繼渠，錫寶下部議。

translations.literal: Ning Hui, son of a garrison battalion corporal Ning Tingyan, killed battalion corporal Zhang Jiqu while collecting a debt; Xibao referred the case to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Hui, son of garrison corporal Ning Tingyan, killed corporal Zhang Jiqu while pressing for repayment of a debt; Xibao referred the case to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 上巡山東，召見，命來京以部屬用。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured Shandong he summoned Xibao for audience and ordered him to the capital for use in a ministry post.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial tour of Shandong the Emperor received him in audience and ordered him to the capital for appointment in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 以大學士阿桂奏，令入四庫全書館自效。

translations.literal: On Grand Secretary Agui's memorial he was ordered to serve in the Siku Quanshu project to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Grand Secretary Agui's recommendation he was assigned to the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries to redeem himself through service.

sentences.zh: 書成，以國子監司業升用。

translations.literal: When the project was completed he was promoted for service as vice director of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was finished he was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 居三年，上以錫寶補司業無期，特授陝西道監察御史。

translations.literal: After three years the Emperor, finding no prospect of Xibao filling the vice directorship, specially appointed him investigating censor for the Shaanxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, with no opening for him as vice director, the Emperor specially appointed him investigating censor for the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 時協辦大學士和珅執政，其奴劉全恃勢營私，衣服、車馬、居室皆踰制。

translations.literal: At that time Assisting Grand Secretary Heshen held power; his bondservant Liu Quan relied on influence for private gain, and his clothing, carriages, and dwelling all exceeded regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting Grand Secretary Heshen was then in power; his bondservant Liu Quan used his master's influence for private gain, with clothing, carriages, and a residence all beyond what regulations allowed.

sentences.zh: 錫寶將論劾，侍郎南匯吳省欽與錫寶同鄉里，聞其事，和珅方從上熱河行在，馳以告和珅，令全毀其室，衣服、車馬有踰制，皆匿無跡。

translations.literal: Xibao was about to impeach him; Vice Minister Wu Shengqin of Nanhui, a fellow townsman, heard of it. Heshen was then with the Emperor at the Rehe palace, and Shengqin hurried to inform him; Heshen ordered Quan to destroy his house, and all items exceeding regulations in clothing and carriages were hidden without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao prepared to impeach Liu Quan; Vice Minister Wu Shengqin of Nanhui, a fellow townsman, learned of it. Heshen was with the Emperor at Rehe; Shengqin rode posthaste to warn him, and Heshen had Quan tear down his house and hide every item that exceeded regulations.

sentences.zh: 錫寶疏至，上詰和珅。

translations.literal: When Xibao's memorial arrived the Emperor interrogated Heshen.
translations.idiomatic: When Xibao's memorial arrived the Emperor questioned Heshen.

sentences.zh: 和珅言平時戒約嚴，或扈從日久漸生事，乞嚴察重懲。

translations.literal: Heshen said he was usually strict in discipline, but that perhaps after long attendance on tour Quan had gradually caused trouble, and begged strict investigation and heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen said he ordinarily kept strict discipline, but that perhaps after long service on tour Quan had gradually misbehaved, and asked that he be strictly investigated and severely punished.

sentences.zh: 乃命留京辦事王大臣召錫寶問狀，又令步軍統領遣官從錫寶至全家察視，無跡，錫寶自承冒昧。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the minister in Beijing to summon Xibao and question him, and also ordered the metropolitan commandant to send officials with Xibao to inspect Quan's household; no trace was found, and Xibao confessed he had been rash.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered a minister in Beijing to question Xibao and sent officials with him to search Quan's house; nothing was found, and Xibao admitted he had acted rashly.

sentences.zh: 上召錫寶詣行在面詰，錫寶奏全倚勢營私，未有實跡，第為和珅「杜漸防微」，乃有此奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Xibao to the traveling palace for personal interrogation; Xibao memorialized that Quan relied on power for private gain though no concrete proof had been found, and that he had memorialized only to help Heshen "check evil at its first appearance."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the traveling palace, Xibao said Quan had certainly abused power though no proof remained, and that his memorial had been meant to help Heshen "nip evil in the bud."

sentences.zh: 复諭軍機大臣、大學士梁國治等覆詢，錫寶又承「杜漸防微」語失當，請治罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor again instructed Grand Councilor and Grand Secretary Liang Guozhi and others to question him further; Xibao again admitted the phrase "check evil at its first appearance" was improper and asked to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned again by Grand Secretary Liang Guozhi and other Grand Councilors, Xibao admitted the "nip evil in the bud" formula was improper and asked for punishment.

sentences.zh: 下部議，當左遷。

translations.literal: Referred to the ministry for deliberation, demotion was appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended demotion.

sentences.zh: 上手詔略言：「平時用人行政，不肯存逆詐億不信之見。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally issued an edict in brief saying: "In ordinary employment of men and conduct of government I am unwilling to harbor suspicions of deceit and distrust.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's personal edict said in part: "In appointing officials and governing the realm I refuse to harbor habitual suspicion and distrust.

sentences.zh: 若委用臣工不能推誠佈公，而猜疑防範，據一時無根之談，遽入人以罪，使天下重足而立、側目而視，斷無此政體。

translations.literal: If in employing ministers I cannot extend sincere openness, but instead suspect and guard against them, and on the basis of groundless talk at a single moment hastily charge men with crimes, so that all under Heaven stand on tiptoe and look askance—there is no such form of government.
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot deal openly with my ministers yet suspect and fence them off, and on a moment's baseless rumor rush to convict a man so that the empire walks in fear—that is no government I would accept.

sentences.zh: 錫寶未察虛實，以書生拘迂之見，託為正言陳奏。

translations.literal: Xibao did not examine truth and falsehood; with the cramped views of a bookish man he put forward this as upright memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao had not verified his facts; in bookish narrowness he had dressed rash speech as loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 姑寬其罰，改革職留任。」

translations.literal: His punishment is temporarily waived; he is transferred to another post and retained in service.
translations.idiomatic: His punishment was waived; he was transferred to another post and kept in service.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-seventh year.

sentences.zh: 仁宗親政，誅和珅，並籍全家，乃追思錫寶直言，諭曰：「故御史曹錫寶，嘗劾和珅奴劉全倚勢營私，家貲豐厚。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took power in person he executed Heshen and confiscated his entire household; he then recalled Xibao's forthright memorial and issued an edict saying: "The late Censor Cao Xibao once impeached Heshen's bondservant Liu Quan for relying on power for private gain and amassing great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong personally assumed rule he executed Heshen and confiscated his household; recalling Xibao's bold memorial, he said: "The late Censor Cao Xibao once impeached Heshen's bondservant Liu Quan for abusing power and amassing great wealth.

sentences.zh: 彼時和珅聲勢薰灼，舉朝無一人敢於糾劾，而錫寶獨能抗辭執奏，不愧諍臣。

translations.literal: At that time Heshen's power filled the court and not a man dared impeach him, yet Xibao alone could speak out in firm memorial—worthy of a remonstrating minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Heshen's influence filled the court and no one dared impeach him, yet Xibao alone spoke out—a true remonstrating minister.

sentences.zh: 今和珅治罪後，並籍全家，貲產至二十馀萬。

translations.literal: Now that Heshen has been punished and his whole household confiscated, his property amounts to more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Heshen has been punished and his household confiscated, his property exceeds two hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 是錫寶所劾不虛，宜加優獎，以旌直言。

translations.literal: Thus what Xibao impeached was not false; he should receive special reward to honor forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao's charges were not false; he should be specially rewarded to honor honest speech.

sentences.zh: 錫寶贈副都御史，其子江視贈官予廕。」

translations.literal: Xibao was posthumously given Vice Censor-in-Chief rank, and his son Jiang was granted hereditary office according to the posthumous rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao was posthumously made Vice Censor-in-Chief, and his son Jiang received hereditary privilege according to that rank.

sentences.zh: 錫寶，一士從子，再世居台省，敢言名。

translations.literal: Xibao was a nephew of Yishi Cong; for two generations the family served in the censorate and won fame for daring speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao was a nephew of Yishi Cong; for two generations the family served at court and was known for outspokenness.

sentences.zh: 家有甕，焚諫草，江嘗乞諸能文者為詩歌，傳一時雲。

translations.literal: The family kept an urn in which memorial drafts were burned; Jiang once asked men of letters to compose poems about it, which were celebrated for a time.
translations.idiomatic: The family kept an urn for burning draft memorials; Jiang once asked literary men to compose poems about it, which circulated widely for a time.

sentences.zh: =謝振定=謝振定，字一齋，一字薌泉，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xie Zhending, styled Yizhai and also Xiangquan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhending, whose courtesy names were Yizhai and Xiangquan, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy, and after leaving the academy was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，考選江南道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was selected as investigating censor for the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he was selected investigating censor for the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 巡視南漕，漕艘阻瓜洲，振定禱於神，風轉順漕艘，人稱「謝公風」。

translations.literal: While inspecting the southern grain transport, transport vessels were blocked at Guazhou; Zhending prayed to the god and the wind shifted; the grain fleet passed, and people called it "Secretary Xie's wind."
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting southern grain transport, he found vessels blocked at Guazhou; Zhending prayed to the river god, the wind turned fair, and the fleet moved—people called it "Secretary Xie's wind."

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷兵科給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to supervising secretary of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was made supervising secretary of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 巡視東城，有乘違制車騁於衢者，執而訊之，則和珅妾弟也，語不遜，振定命痛笞之，遂焚其車。

translations.literal: While inspecting the eastern city he found someone driving an illegal carriage racing through the streets; he seized and questioned him—it was Heshen's wife's younger brother. He spoke insolently; Zhending ordered him beaten severely and burned the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the eastern city he seized a man driving an illegal carriage at speed—it was Heshen's brother-in-law. When the man was insolent, Zhending had him beaten and burned the carriage.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此車豈堪宰相坐耶？」

translations.literal: He said: "How could such a carriage be fit for a grand secretary to sit in?"
translations.idiomatic: He declared: "How could a carriage like this be fit for a grand secretary?"

sentences.zh: 居數日，給事中王鍾健希和珅意，假他事劾振定，奪職。

translations.literal: Several days later Supervising Secretary Wang Zhongjian, courting Heshen's favor, impeached Zhending on another pretext and he was deprived of office.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Supervising Secretary Wang Zhongjian, seeking Heshen's favor, impeached Zhending on another charge and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 和珅敗，嘉慶五年，起授禮部主事。

translations.literal: After Heshen's fall, in the fifth year of Jiaqing he was recalled and appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Heshen's downfall, in the fifth year of Jiaqing he was recalled as principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遷員外郎，充坐糧廳，監收漕糧，裁革陋規，兌運肅然。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director, served in the grain-receipt office, supervised collection of tribute grain, abolished corrupt customs, and transport became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director, he served in the grain-receipt office, supervised tribute grain collection, cut abusive fees, and transport became orderly.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 道光中，振定子興嶢，官河南裕州知州。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang reign Zhending's son Xingyao served as magistrate of Yuzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daoguang reign his son Xingyao was magistrate of Yuzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 以卓薦引見，循例奏姓名、裡貫。

translations.literal: Recommended for outstanding merit he was presented at court and, according to precedent, reported his name and native place.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for outstanding service he was presented at court and, by precedent, gave his name and native place.

sentences.zh: 宣宗問：「爾湖南人，乃能為京師語，何也？」

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor asked: "You are a Hunan man—how can you speak the capital dialect?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong asked: "You are from Hunan—how is it you speak the capital dialect?"

sentences.zh: 興嶢對言：「臣父振定官御史，臣生長京師。」

translations.literal: Xingyao answered: "My father Zhending was a censor; I grew up in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Xingyao replied: "My father Zhending served as a censor; I grew up in the capital."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「爾乃燒車御史子耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "So you are the son of the censor who burned the carriage?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Then you are the son of the carriage-burning censor?"

sentences.zh: 因褒勉甚至。

translations.literal: He therefore praised and encouraged him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He praised and encouraged him warmly.

sentences.zh: 明日，語軍機大臣：「朕少聞燒車御史事，昨乃見其子。」

translations.literal: The next day he told the Grand Councilors: "In my youth I heard of the carriage-burning censor; yesterday I met his son."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told the Grand Councilors: "I heard of the carriage-burning censor in my youth; yesterday I saw his son."

sentences.zh: 命擢興嶢敘州知府。

translations.literal: He ordered Xingyao promoted to prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xingyao promoted to prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: =錢灃=錢灃，字東注，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Qian Feng, styled Dongzhu, was a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Feng, whose courtesy name was Dongzhu, came from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy, and after leaving the academy was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，考選江南道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was selected as investigating censor for the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he was selected investigating censor for the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 甘肅冒賑折捐事發，主其事者為甘肅布政使王亶望，時已遷浙江巡撫，坐誅，總督勒爾謹及諸府縣吏死者數十人，事具亶望傳。

translations.literal: When the Gansu fraudulent relief and grain-sale scandal broke, the chief culprit was Gansu Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Danwang, who had already been transferred to Zhejiang governor and was executed; Governor-General Le'erjin and dozens of prefectural and county officials died; the affair is recorded in Danwang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gansu fraudulent relief and diverted-grain scandal erupted, the chief figure was Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Danwang, by then Zhejiang governor; he was executed, Governor-General Le'erjin and dozens of prefectural and county officials died—the affair is detailed in Danwang's biography.

sentences.zh: 陝西巡撫畢沅嘗兩署陝甘總督，獨置不問。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan had twice acted as Shaan-Gan governor-general and was alone left unquestioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Governor Bi Yuan had twice served as acting Shaan-Gan governor-general yet was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 灃疏言：「冒賑折捐，固由亶望骫法，但亶望為布政使時，沅兩署總督，近在同城，豈無聞見？

translations.literal: Feng memorialized: "The fraudulent relief and diverted grain were certainly due to Danwang's violation of law, but when Danwang was provincial administration commissioner Yuan twice acted as governor-general and lived in the same city—could he have heard nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Feng memorialized: "The fraud was certainly Danwang's doing, yet when Danwang was provincial commissioner Bi Yuan twice acted as governor-general in the same city—could he have known nothing?

sentences.zh: 使沅早發其奸，則播惡不至如此之甚；

translations.literal: Had Yuan exposed the crime early, the spread of evil would not have been so severe;
translations.idiomatic: Had Yuan exposed the crime early, the evil would not have spread so far;

sentences.zh: 即陷於刑闢者，亦不至如此之多。

translations.literal: even those who fell under punishment would not have been so numerous.
translations.idiomatic: nor would so many have been condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢謂其利令智昏，甘受所餌，惟是瞻徇回護，不肯舉發，甚非大臣居心之道。

translations.literal: I dare not say he was blinded by profit and accepted bribes, but in looking on and shielding and refusing to report, he fell far short of how a great minister should conduct himself.
translations.idiomatic: I do not say he was bribed, but in shielding wrongdoing and refusing to report he failed the standard of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 請比捏結各員治罪。」

translations.literal: I request that he be punished like those who fabricated the scheme."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be punished like the conspirators."

sentences.zh: 上為詰責沅，降秩視三品，事具沅傳。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Yuan and reduced his rank to third grade; the affair is recorded in Yuan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Bi Yuan and reduced him to third rank; the affair is recorded in his biography.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，灃疏劾山東巡撫國泰、布政使於易簡吏治廢弛，貪婪無饜，各州縣庫皆虧缺，上命大學士和珅、左都御史劉墉率灃往按。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year Feng memorialized impeaching Shandong Governor Guotai and Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yijian for lax government and insatiable greed; treasuries in every prefecture and county were in deficit. The Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Heshen and Left Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong to lead Feng in investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year Feng impeached Shandong Governor Guotai and Commissioner Yu Yijian for ruined governance and insatiable greed; treasuries throughout the province were short. The Emperor sent Grand Secretary Heshen and Left Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong with Feng to investigate.

sentences.zh: 和珅庇國泰，怵灃，灃不為撓。

translations.literal: Heshen shielded Guotai and tried to intimidate Feng, but Feng would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen protected Guotai and tried to intimidate Feng, who would not bend.

sentences.zh: 至山東，發歷城縣庫驗帑銀。

translations.literal: Arriving in Shandong they opened the Licheng county treasury to verify the silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong they opened the Licheng county treasury to verify the silver.

sentences.zh: 故事，帑銀以五十兩為一鋌，市銀則否。

translations.literal: By precedent treasury silver came in ingots of fifty taels each; market silver did not.
translations.idiomatic: By rule treasury silver was cast in fifty-tael ingots; market silver was not.

sentences.zh: 國泰聞使者將至，假市銀補庫。

translations.literal: Guotai, hearing the investigators were coming, borrowed market silver to fill the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the investigators were coming, Guotai borrowed market silver to pad the treasury.

sentences.zh: 灃按問得其狀，召商還所假，庫為之空。

translations.literal: Feng questioned and learned the facts, summoned the merchants to return what had been borrowed, and the treasury was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Feng established the facts, made the merchants reclaim their silver, and the treasury stood empty.

sentences.zh: 复按章丘、東平、益都三州縣庫，皆虧缺如灃言。

translations.literal: They then inspected the treasuries of Zhangqiu, Dongping, and Yidu; all showed deficits as Feng had said.
translations.idiomatic: They inspected Zhangqiu, Dongping, and Yidu as well; every treasury was short, just as Feng had charged.

sentences.zh: 國泰、易簡罪至死，和珅不能護也。

translations.literal: Guotai and Yijian were sentenced to death; Heshen could not protect them.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai and Yijian were sentenced to death; Heshen could not save them.

sentences.zh: 上旌灃直言，擢通政司參議。

translations.literal: The Emperor honored Feng's forthright speech and promoted him to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised Feng's honesty and promoted him to Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 再遷通政司副使。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 出督湖南學政，灃持正，得士為盛。

translations.literal: He went out as Hunan education commissioner; Feng was upright and the scholars he produced were outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Hunan education commissioner, Feng was strict and just and produced many excellent scholars.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，任滿，命留任。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, when his term expired, he was ordered to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year, when his term ended, he was ordered to stay on.

sentences.zh: 湖北荊州水壞城郭，孝感土豪殺饑民。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou, Hubei, floods destroyed the city walls; in Xiaogan local bullies killed famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: Floods destroyed the walls of Jingzhou in Hubei; in Xiaogan local bullies killed famine victims.

sentences.zh: 上責灃在鄰省何不以聞，下部議。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Feng for not reporting this though he was in a neighboring province, and referred him to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Feng for failing to report these events though he was in a neighboring province, and referred him to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 諸生或匿喪赴試，又有上違禁書籍者。

translations.literal: Some licentiates concealed mourning to take the examination, and some presented forbidden books.
translations.idiomatic: Some licentiates hid deaths in the family to sit for examinations, and some submitted forbidden books.

sentences.zh: 灃按治未竟，聞親喪去官，以事屬巡撫浦霖。

translations.literal: Feng had not finished investigating when he left office on his father's death and turned the matter over to Governor Pulín.
translations.idiomatic: Feng had not finished the investigation when he left on his father's death and left the matter to Governor Pulín.

sentences.zh: 霖遂並劾灃，坐奪職。

translations.literal: Pulín then impeached Feng as well and he was deprived of office.
translations.idiomatic: Pulín then impeached Feng too, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 上命左授六部主事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him demoted to principal clerk in one of the six ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor demoted him to principal clerk in one of the six ministries.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，灃服除，詣京師，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when his mourning ended, Feng came to the capital and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year, after mourning, Feng came to the capital and was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 引見，即擢員外郎。

translations.literal: At audience he was immediately promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he was immediately promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 复除湖廣道監察御史。

translations.literal: He was again appointed investigating censor for the Huguang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made investigating censor for the Huguang circuit.

sentences.zh: 時和珅愈專政，大學士阿桂、王杰，尚書董誥、福長安與同為軍機大臣，不相能，入直恆異處。

translations.literal: At that time Heshen's power grew ever greater; Grand Secretaries Agui and Wang Jie and Ministers Dong Gao and Fu Chang'an served with him on the Grand Council but did not get along, and on entering duty they usually stayed in separate places.
translations.idiomatic: By then Heshen dominated government; Grand Secretaries Agui and Wang Jie and Ministers Dong Gao and Fu Chang'an sat on the Grand Council with him but could not work together, each keeping to a separate office.

sentences.zh: 灃疏言：「我朝設立軍機處，大臣與其職者，皆萃止其中，庸以集思廣益，仰贊高深。

translations.literal: Feng memorialized: "Our dynasty established the Grand Council so that ministers holding its duties would all gather within it, thereby pooling counsel to broaden benefit and assist the throne's lofty deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Feng memorialized: "The Grand Council was established so that all ministers who shared its duties would gather in one place, pooling counsel to assist the throne.

sentences.zh: 地一則勢無所分，居同則情可共見。

translations.literal: One place means power cannot be divided; dwelling together means intentions can be seen together.
translations.idiomatic: One location prevents divided power; shared quarters let intentions be seen plainly.

sentences.zh: 即各司諮事畫，亦有定所。

translations.literal: Even when various offices consult and draft, there are fixed places for this.
translations.idiomatic: Even routine consultation and drafting have fixed places.

sentences.zh: 近日惟阿桂每日入止軍機處；

translations.literal: Recently only Agui enters and remains in the Grand Council each day;
translations.idiomatic: Lately only Agui enters the Grand Council daily and remains there;

sentences.zh: 和珅或止內右門內直廬，或止隆宗門外近造辦處直廬；

translations.literal: Heshen sometimes stays in the inner right gate duty room, or in the duty room near the construction office outside Longzong Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Heshen sometimes stays in the duty room inside the inner right gate, or in the room near the construction office outside Longzong Gate;

sentences.zh: 王杰、董誥則止於南書房；

translations.literal: Wang Jie and Dong Gao stay only in the Southern Study;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie and Dong Gao remain only in the Southern Study;

sentences.zh: 福長安則止於造辦處。

translations.literal: Fu Chang'an stays only at the construction office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang'an stays only at the construction office.

sentences.zh: 每日召對，聯行而入，退即各還所處。

translations.literal: Each day when summoned to audience they enter in a group, but on retiring each returns to his own place.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they enter together for audience, then withdraw to separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 雖亦有時暫至軍機處，而事過輒起。

translations.literal: Although they sometimes go briefly to the Grand Council, they rise and leave as soon as the business is done.
translations.idiomatic: They may visit the Grand Council briefly, but leave as soon as the matter is finished.

sentences.zh: 各司諮事畫，趨步多歧。

translations.literal: When various offices consulted and drafted, their comings and goings took many different paths.
translations.idiomatic: When various offices brought business for consultation and drafting, officials came and went by many different routes.

sentences.zh: 皇上乾行之健，離照之明，大小臣工戴德懷刑，浹於肌髓，決不至因此遂啟朋黨角立之漸。

translations.literal: The Emperor's vigorous conduct is like Heaven's strength, his illumination like the sun's radiance; great and small officials bear his virtue and fear his punishments, soaked to the marrow—this will certainly not therefore give rise to the first steps of factional rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's vigor and clarity inspire awe throughout the bureaucracy; this reform will not, as feared, open the door to factional rivalry.

sentences.zh: 然世宗憲皇帝以來，及皇上御極之久，軍機大臣萃止無渙，未嘗纖芥有他。

translations.literal: Yet from the time of the Shizong Emperor down through the long years of Your Majesty's reign, Grand Councilors have gathered without dispersing and never had the slightest discord.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yongzheng Emperor to Your Majesty's long reign, Grand Councilors have always gathered together without the slightest friction.

sentences.zh: 由前律後，不應聽其輕更。

translations.literal: Following precedent, this should not be lightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent should not be lightly overturned.

sentences.zh: 內右門內切近禁寢，向因有養心殿帶領引見事，須先一兩刻預備。

translations.literal: Inside the inner right gate lies close to the forbidden quarters; because audiences at the Hall of Mental Cultivation require leading in, one or two quarters' advance preparation is needed.
translations.idiomatic: The duty room inside the inner right gate lies close to the imperial residence; because audiences at the Hall of Mental Cultivation require advance preparation, an hour or two of lead time is needed.

sentences.zh: 恩加大臣，不令與各官露立，是以設廬許得暫止。

translations.literal: In grace to great ministers, they are not made to stand in the open with other officials, and therefore lodges were set up where they might pause briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Out of consideration for great ministers, who should not stand exposed with ordinary officials, lodges were provided for brief rest.

sentences.zh: 不應於未辨色之前，一大臣入止，而隨從軍機司員亦更入更出。

translations.literal: They should not, before dawn has broken, have one great minister enter and remain while Grand Council clerks come and go in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one minister should not enter before dawn while Grand Council clerks stream in and out.

sentences.zh: 為日既久，不能不與內監相狎。

translations.literal: Over a long period they cannot avoid growing familiar with eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Over time they cannot avoid growing familiar with palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 萬一有無知如高雲從者，雖立正刑闢，而所絓已多，杜漸宜早。

translations.literal: If by chance there should be someone as ignorant as Gao Yuncong, though he might be executed at once, much harm would already have been done—checking evil early is best.
translations.idiomatic: Should another fool like Gao Yuncong appear, even immediate execution would come too late; evil is best checked early.

sentences.zh: 至南書房備幾暇顧問，俟軍機事畢，入直未遲；

translations.literal: As for the Southern Study, it is prepared for leisure consultation; after Grand Council business is done, entering duty there is not late;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Study serves for informal consultation; entering duty there after Grand Council business is finished would not be late;

sentences.zh: 若隆宗門外直廬及造辦處，則各色應差皆得覘聽於外，大臣於中治事，亦屬過褻。

translations.literal: but duty rooms outside Longzong Gate and at the construction office allow all sorts of attendants to listen from outside while ministers conduct business within—this is also overly familiar.
translations.idiomatic: but duty rooms outside Longzong Gate and at the construction office let all manner of attendants eavesdrop while ministers work inside—an improper intimacy.

sentences.zh: 請敕諸大臣仍照舊規同止軍機處，庶匪懈之忱，各申五夜；

translations.literal: I beg that the great ministers be ordered to abide by the old rule and remain together at the Grand Council, so that the spirit of diligence may be expressed through the five watches of the night;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ministers return to the old rule and remain together at the Grand Council, keeping vigil through the night watches;

sentences.zh: 協恭之雅，共勵一堂。

translations.literal: and the elegance of cooperative harmony may be encouraged in one hall.
translations.idiomatic: and sustaining cooperative harmony in one hall.

sentences.zh: 其圓明園治事，和珅、福長安止於如意門外南順牆東向直廬，王杰、董誥止於南書房直廬，並請敕更正。」

translations.literal: For business at the Yuanming Garden, Heshen and Fu Chang'an stay only in the east-facing duty room south of the outer wall at Ruyi Gate; Wang Jie and Dong Gao stay only in the Southern Study duty room—please order these corrected as well.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuanming Garden, Heshen and Fu Chang'an should not remain only in the east-facing lodge south of Ruyi Gate, nor Wang Jie and Dong Gao only in the Southern Study lodge—I ask that these arrangements be corrected too.

sentences.zh: 上為申誡諸大臣，並命灃稽察軍機處。

translations.literal: The Emperor admonished the great ministers and ordered Feng to inspect the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admonished the ministers and ordered Feng to inspect the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 和珅素惡灃，至是尤深嗛之。

translations.literal: Heshen had long hated Feng; from this time he hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen had long hated Feng; from this point his hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 上夙許其持正，度未可遽傾，凡遇勞苦事多委之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long approved his uprightness and judged that he could not be quickly overthrown; whenever arduous tasks arose he often assigned them to Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long valued his integrity and would not let him be destroyed outright; difficult tasks were often assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 灃貧，衣裘薄，宵興晡散，遂得疾。

translations.literal: Feng was poor; his fur coat was thin; he rose before dawn and dispersed in late afternoon, and thus fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was poor and thinly clad; rising before dawn and working until late afternoon, he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 六十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixtieth year.

sentences.zh: 或謂灃將劾和珅，和珅實酖之。

translations.literal: Some say Feng was about to impeach Heshen and that Heshen actually poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Feng was preparing to impeach Heshen and that Heshen poisoned him.

sentences.zh: =尹壯圖=尹壯圖，字楚珍，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhuangtu, styled Chuzhen, was a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuangtu, whose courtesy name was Chuzhen, came from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and became a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he took his jinshi degree and became a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館，授禮部主事。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the academy he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the academy he was made principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，考選江南道監察御史，轉京畿道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was selected as investigating censor for the Jiangnan circuit and transferred to the capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he was selected investigating censor for the Jiangnan circuit and transferred to the capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 三遷至內閣學士，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court, concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through three promotions to Grand Secretary of the Inner Court, concurrently Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 高宗季年，督撫坐譴，或令繳罰項貸罪，壯圖以為非政體。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong Emperor's later years, when governors-general and governors were punished, some were allowed to pay fines in lieu of punishment; Zhuangtu held that this was not sound government.
translations.idiomatic: In the Emperor's later years, punished governors-general and governors were sometimes allowed to pay fines instead of facing dismissal; Zhuangtu held this was unsound.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，上疏言：「督撫自蹈愆尤，聖恩不即罷斥，罰銀若干萬充公，亦有督撫自請認罰若干萬者。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he memorialized: "When governors-general and governors themselves commit faults, if the sacred grace does not immediately dismiss them but fines them several tens of thousands for confiscation, some governors-general and governors also volunteer fines of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year he memorialized: "When governors-general and governors err, instead of dismissal the court accepts fines of tens of thousands of taels, and some officials volunteer such fines themselves.

sentences.zh: 在桀驁者藉口以快其饕餮之私，即清廉者亦不得不望屬員之佽助。

translations.literal: The arrogant use this as a pretext to satisfy gluttonous greed; even the upright must look to subordinates for assistance.
translations.idiomatic: The corrupt use this to feed their greed; even honest men must lean on subordinates for help.

sentences.zh: 日後遇有虧空營私重案，不容不曲為庇護。

translations.literal: Later, when grave cases of deficit and private gain arise, they cannot but bend to shield wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when serious cases of embezzlement arise, they cannot but cover for one another.

sentences.zh: 是罰銀雖嚴，不惟無以動其愧懼之心，且潛生其玩易之念，請永停此例。

translations.literal: Thus although the fine is severe, it not only fails to stir shame and fear but secretly breeds contempt; I beg that this practice be permanently stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fines may look severe, yet they neither inspire shame nor deter wrongdoing; I ask that the practice be abolished.

sentences.zh: 如才具平常者，或即罷斥，或用京職，毋許再膺外任。」

translations.literal: For those of ordinary talent, either dismiss them at once or employ them in capital posts, and do not allow them to hold provincial office again."
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre officials should be dismissed or kept in the capital, not sent out to the provinces again."

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「壯圖請停罰銀例，不為無見。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Zhuangtu's request to stop the fine practice is not without insight.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "Zhuangtu's objection to fines is not without point.

sentences.zh: 朕以督撫一時不能得人，棄瑕錄用，酌示薄懲。

translations.literal: I, because governors-general and governors cannot at once be found without flaw, overlook faults and employ them, showing a light punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because suitable governors are hard to find, I overlook faults and impose light fines.

sentences.zh: 但督撫等或有昧良負恩，以措辦官項為辭，需索屬員；

translations.literal: But governors-general and others may, ungrateful for grace, use the pretext of raising official funds to extort subordinates;
translations.idiomatic: Yet some may abuse the system, extorting subordinates under the pretext of raising official funds;

sentences.zh: 而屬員亦藉此斂派逢迎，此亦不能保其必無。

translations.literal: and subordinates also use this to levy and curry favor—this too cannot be guaranteed never to happen.
translations.idiomatic: and subordinates levy and flatter in turn—this too cannot be ruled out.

sentences.zh: 壯圖既為此奏，自必確有見聞，令指實覆奏。」

translations.literal: Since Zhuangtu has memorialized thus, he must have concrete knowledge; I order him to report facts in a follow-up memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhuangtu has raised this, he must have evidence; I order him to report specifics.

sentences.zh: 壯圖覆奏：「各督撫聲名狼藉，吏治廢弛。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu replied: "Every governor-general and governor has a notorious reputation; official discipline is lax.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu replied: "Governors-general and governors are notorious; governance is in ruins.

sentences.zh: 臣經過地方，體察官吏賢否，商民半皆蹙額興嘆。

translations.literal: Where I passed I observed which officials were worthy; merchants and commoners mostly knit their brows and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling through the provinces I observed officials and found merchants and commoners knitting their brows and sighing.

sentences.zh: 各省風氣，大抵皆然。

translations.literal: The temper of every province is largely the same.
translations.idiomatic: The condition is much the same everywhere.

sentences.zh: 請旨簡派滿洲大臣同臣往各省密查虧空。」

translations.literal: I beg that Manchu ministers be selected to go with me to each province for secret investigation of deficits."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Manchu ministers be sent with me to investigate deficits secretly in each province."

sentences.zh: 上复諭曰：「壯圖覆奏，並未指實。

translations.literal: The Emperor again instructed: "Zhuangtu's reply still did not name anyone.
