translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied again: "Your reply still names no one.

sentences.zh: 至稱經過諸省商民蹙額興嘆，竟似居今之世，民不堪命。

translations.literal: To say that merchants and commoners along the route knit their brows and sigh makes it sound as if in the present age the people cannot bear their lot.
translations.idiomatic: To say merchants everywhere knit their brows and sigh makes it sound as if the people cannot endure their lives.

sentences.zh: 此聞自何人，見於何處，仍令指實覆奏。」

translations.literal: From whom did you hear this, and where did you see it? I still order you to report facts in a follow-up memorial.
translations.idiomatic: From whom did you hear this and where did you see it? Report facts again.

sentences.zh: 壯圖再覆奏，自承措詞過當，請治罪。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu memorialized again, confessing his language was excessive and asking to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu memorialized again, admitting his words were excessive and asking for punishment.

sentences.zh: 上命戶部侍郎慶成偕壯圖赴山西察倉庫，始大同府庫，次山西布政使庫，皆無虧。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Qing Cheng to go with Zhuangtu to inspect granaries and treasuries in Shanxi, first at Datong prefecture, then at the provincial administration commissioner's treasury—both showed no deficit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Vice Minister Qing Cheng with Zhuangtu to inspect Shanxi treasuries, beginning at Datong and then the provincial treasury—both were sound.

sentences.zh: 壯圖請還京治罪。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu asked to return to the capital to accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu asked to return to the capital for punishment.

sentences.zh: 上命慶成偕壯圖再赴直隸、山東、江南諸省。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Qing Cheng to go with Zhuangtu again to Zhili, Shandong, and Jiangnan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered them to continue to Zhili, Shandong, and Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 慶成所至，輒遊宴數日，乃發倉庫校覈，歷直隸布政使及正定、蘭山、山陽諸府縣，皆無虧。

translations.literal: Wherever Qing Cheng arrived he would feast for several days before opening granaries and treasuries for verification; through Zhili provincial administration and Zhengding, Lanshan, Shanyang and other prefectures and counties, all showed no deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Cheng feasted for days at each stop before inspecting treasuries; through Zhili and numerous prefectures and counties, all were sound.

sentences.zh: 上寄諭壯圖，問途中見商民蹙額興嘆狀否。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent instructions to Zhuangtu asking whether along the route he had seen merchants knitting their brows and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Zhuangtu whether he had seen merchants knitting their brows and sighing along the way.

sentences.zh: 壯圖覆奏，言目見商民樂業，絕無蹙額興嘆情事。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu replied that he had seen merchants content in their occupations and absolutely no knitting of brows or sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu replied that merchants were prospering and he saw no such distress.

sentences.zh: 上又令慶成傳旨，令其指實二三人，毋更含糊支飾。

translations.literal: The Emperor again had Qing Cheng transmit an edict ordering him to name two or three men specifically and not evade with vague words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again ordered him to name two or three specific men and stop equivocating.

sentences.zh: 壯圖自承虛誑，奏請治罪。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu confessed he had spoken falsely and memorialized asking to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu confessed he had lied and asked for punishment.

sentences.zh: 尋复察蘇州布政使庫，亦無虧。

translations.literal: Soon they also inspected the Suzhou provincial administration commissioner's treasury; again no deficit.
translations.idiomatic: They also inspected the Suzhou provincial treasury; again no deficit.

sentences.zh: 還京，下刑部治罪，比挾詐欺公、妄生異議律，坐斬決。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was sent to the Board of Punishments; by the statute on using fraud to deceive the public and rashly raising dissent, he was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he was tried by the Board of Punishments and sentenced to decapitation for fraud and reckless dissent.

sentences.zh: 上謂壯圖逞臆妄言，亦不妨以謗為規，不必遽加重罪，命左授內閣侍讀。

translations.literal: The Emperor said Zhuangtu had spoken from reckless imagination, yet this did not prevent taking slander as remonstrance; there was no need hastily to add grave punishment—he was demoted to left reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said Zhuangtu had spoken rashly, yet honest error might still serve as remonstrance; he was demoted to Grand Secretariat reader rather than executed.

sentences.zh: 繼又以侍讀缺少，改禮部主事。

translations.literal: Soon, because a reader's post was vacant, he was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When a reader's post fell vacant he was made principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 壯圖以母老乞歸。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu begged to return home because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu asked to retire because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，仁宗親政，召詣京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when the Renzong Emperor took power in person, he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, when Emperor Renzong personally assumed rule, Zhuangtu was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 壯圖仍以母老乞歸，上賜其母大緞兩端，加壯圖給事中銜，賜奏事摺匣，命得上章言事。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu again begged to return because his mother was old; the Emperor gave his mother two bolts of heavy silk, added supervising secretary rank for Zhuangtu, bestowed a memorial folder, and ordered him to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He again pleaded his mother's age; the Emperor gave his mother silk, granted him supervising secretary rank, a memorial folder, and permission to memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 壯圖未行，复上疏請清覈各省陋規，明定科條，上以為不可行。

translations.literal: Before departing Zhuangtu again memorialized requesting thorough elimination of abusive provincial customs and clear regulations; the Emperor held this impracticable.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he memorialized to abolish abusive provincial customs; the Emperor ruled it impracticable.

sentences.zh: 既歸，疏請拔真才，儲實用，大要謂：「保舉未定處分，當下吏部嚴立科條；

translations.literal: After returning home he memorialized requesting selection of true talent and storage of practical men, saying in substance: "When recommendations are made but punishment is undecided, the Ministry of Personnel should strictly establish regulations;
translations.idiomatic: At home he memorialized on selecting true talent, urging among other things that "when recommendations are pending punishment, the Ministry of Personnel should set strict rules;

sentences.zh: 科埸或通關節，當將房考落卷送主司搜閱。

translations.literal: if in the examination halls passages are smuggled through, rejected papers should be sent to the chief examiner for search and review.
translations.idiomatic: if examination fraud occurs, rejected papers should be sent to the chief examiner for review.

sentences.zh: 其尤要者，謂六部滿洲司員案，文義多未曉暢，當嚴督令習經書通文理；

translations.literal: Most important, he said that in the six ministries Manchu clerks often could not understand the literary sense of cases and should be strictly supervised to study the classics and master literary principles;
translations.idiomatic: He especially urged that Manchu clerks in the six ministries, often unable to grasp case documents, be made to study the classics;

sentences.zh: 鄉會試加廣名額，司員先侭科甲挑補。」

translations.literal: provincial and metropolitan quotas should be increased, and clerks should first be chosen from jinshi and presented graduates for supplementation.
translations.idiomatic: examination quotas should be enlarged and clerks chosen first from degree holders.

sentences.zh: 下軍機大臣議，奏謂惟房考落卷送主司搜閱，事近可行，補入科場條例。

translations.literal: The Grand Council deliberated and memorialized that only sending rejected papers to the chief examiner for search and review was nearly feasible; this was added to examination regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council found only the rejected-paper review feasible and added it to examination regulations.

sentences.zh: 雲南巡撫初彭齡乞養歸，壯圖疏請留，上不允。

translations.literal: When Yunnan Governor Chu Pengling begged to retire for his parents' care, Zhuangtu memorialized asking that he be retained; the Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan Governor Chu Pengling asked to retire to care for his parents, Zhuangtu asked that he be kept; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 別疏復申前議，謂滿洲子弟十五六歲前專責習經書通文理，再習騎射繙譯。

translations.literal: In another memorial he again pressed his earlier views, saying Manchu youths before fifteen or sixteen should be required to study the classics and master literary principles, then study riding, archery, and translation.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he again urged that Manchu boys before fifteen or sixteen study the classics first, then riding, archery, and translation.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「壯圖以前嘗駁飭之事復行瀆陳，更張本朝成法。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Zhuangtu repeats matters he was once rebuked for, again offering irreverent memorials and seeking to overturn the established laws of this dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said Zhuangtu was repeating rejected proposals and seeking to overturn dynastic law.

sentences.zh: 下雲南巡撫伊桑阿傳旨申飭。」

translations.literal: He ordered Yunnan Governor Yisang'a to transmit an edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yunnan Governor Yisang'a to rebuke him by edict.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏言：「天下萬幾，皆皇上獨理。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized: "All the myriad affairs of the empire are handled by the Emperor alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he memorialized: "All affairs of state are handled by the Emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 內外諸臣不過浮沉旅進旅退之中，無能匡扶弼亮。

translations.literal: Within and outside, the various ministers merely drift forward and back in the tide of office, unable to support or assist.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers within and without merely drift with office, unable to support or counsel.

sentences.zh: 請於內之卿貳、翰詹、科道，外之籓、臬、道、府，慎選二十人，輪直內廷。

translations.literal: I beg that from among vice ministers, Hanlin, and censors within, and governors, intendants, and prefects without, twenty men be carefully chosen to serve in rotation within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that twenty men be chosen from vice ministers, Hanlin, censors, governors, and prefects to serve in rotation inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 每日奏章諭旨，盡心檢校，有疏忽偏倚之處，許就近詳辨可否。」

translations.literal: Each day they should carefully examine memorials and edicts; where there is negligence or bias, they should be allowed to discuss nearby whether matters are feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they should review memorials and edicts and discuss errors of negligence or bias on the spot.

sentences.zh: 上責：「壯圖言皆迂闊紕謬，斷不可行。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him: "Everything Zhuangtu says is cramped, erroneous, and confused—absolutely impracticable.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him: "Everything you say is impracticable nonsense.

sentences.zh: 若如所奏，直於軍機大臣外復設內軍機，成何政體？」

translations.literal: If carried out as memorialized, it would mean setting up an inner Grand Council besides the Grand Council—what sort of government would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: As you propose, I would have an inner Grand Council beside the Grand Council—what government would that be?"

sentences.zh: 因及雲南布政使陳孝升、道員薩榮安方以冒銷軍需被罪，令巡撫那彥寶詰壯圖，何無一言奏及。

translations.literal: He also mentioned that Yunnan Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Xiaosheng and Circuit Intendant Sa Rong'an were being punished for fraudulent military supplies, and ordered Governor Nayenbao to question Zhuangtu why he had not memorialized on this.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that Yunnan officials were being punished for fraudulent military supplies and asked why Zhuangtu had not reported it.

sentences.zh: 壯圖言以不得孝升等確據，未敢入告，仍請議處，上命寬之。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu said he had lacked firm evidence on Xiaosheng and others and dared not report; he still asked to be punished, and the Emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu said he lacked proof and had not dared report; he still asked for punishment, and the Emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：高宗中年後，遇有言事者，遣大臣按治，輒命其參與。

translations.literal: Commentary says: After the Gaozong Emperor reached mid-life, whenever memorialists appeared he sent great ministers to investigate and always ordered them to participate.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In his middle years, whenever someone memorialized the throne the Gaozong Emperor sent ministers to investigate and usually ordered the memorialist to take part.

sentences.zh: 光鼐既將坐譴，卒得自白，阿桂之賢也。

translations.literal: Guangnai was about to be punished yet finally cleared himself—this was Agui's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnai was on the verge of punishment yet finally vindicated himself—credit Agui's integrity.

sentences.zh: 灃劾國泰發庫藏掩覆，論者謂劉墉密與灃商榷，蓋亦有力焉。

translations.literal: When Feng impeached Guotai and exposed the treasury cover-up, commentators say Liu Yong secretly consulted with Feng—he too had force.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's exposure of Guotai's padded treasury is said to have had Liu Yong's secret support.

sentences.zh: 漱芳、錫寶、壯圖皆不能實其言，大臣怙寵亂政，民迫於飢寒，卒成禍亂。

translations.literal: Shufang, Xibao, and Zhuangtu could none of them substantiate their words; great ministers relied on favor to disorder government, and the people, driven by hunger and cold, finally brought calamity and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shufang, Xibao, and Zhuangtu could not prove their charges; favored ministers corrupted government, and people driven by hunger and cold finally rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，古昔聖王兢兢，重畏民碞，良有以也！

translations.literal: Alas! The sage kings of old were cautious and in awe of the people's complaints—for good reason!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! The ancient sage kings trembled before the people's complaints—and rightly so!
